summary: Tested both backend (8 pytest tests, 100% pass) and frontend Nokia launcher UI (all critical flows pass). Backend /api/apps returns 19 apps with correct categorization. Frontend: 50/50 split is exact (0.50 ratio), navigation via keys 2/8 works, key 5 opens menu, key # returns to home, app list scrolls correctly, important apps are prominent and unimportant apps are dimmed (text-white/40), status bar shows signal/wifi/battery/time/date, T9 letters displayed on keypad.

issues: Minor: * key shows '+' and 0 key shows '_' instead of traditional Nokia 3310 conventions (* = symbols, 0 = space). Acceptable variant but not strictly authentic.
Left/Right navigation (keys 4 and 6) wired in Keypad.jsx but NokiaLauncher's handleNavigation only handles 'up'/'down'. Currently no-op which is fine for vertical menu but unused branches exist.

action_items: Optional: Add left/right navigation handling in NokiaLauncher.handleNavigation, or remove the action wiring for keys 4/6 to be consistent.
Optional: T9 letters mapping for * and 0 could be made more Nokia-authentic ('*' = symbols, '0' = space).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: /api/apps returns hardcoded list - acceptable for MVP but could read from DB; preferences endpoint correctly excludes _id (uses projection {'_id': 0}).
NokiaLauncher.jsx menu item 'Contacts' and 'Messages' actions only console.log - not user-facing issue but no navigation occurs on selecting them from home.
Selecting an app in menu view only logs to console; no app-detail view or action (acknowledged in code comment 'Here you could open the app').
Tap-on-key visual feedback (activeKey state) only lasts 75ms — works but very subtle; in test the toggled class change wasn't observed due to timing (button still highlights via active: pseudo).
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_youtube preference in MongoDB via POST /api/apps/preferences during persistence verification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_nokia_api.py covers root, /api/apps (structure/categorization), and preferences GET/POST with persistence verification. Frontend UI tested with mobile viewport (390x844) — confirmed 50/50 split, full keypad rendering, T9 navigation, menu open/close, and important vs unimportant app styling. Home screen has 3 items (Menu, Contacts, Messages); only Menu has functional action.
